title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Food & Agriculture
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Researchers took root on the refrigeration controllers behind cold stores and supermarkets — then turned the cooling off while the display kept reading normal
items.content_text: Claroty’s Team82 published research on 11–12 August covering two of the most widely deployed refrigeration supervisory platforms in food retail, cold storage and warehousing: the Copeland XWEB Pro family and the Danfoss AK-SM 800A. They reported 23 CVEs in Copeland XWEB Pro, 21 of them rated high severity, plus three in the Danfoss controller; CVE-2026-24452 and CVE-2026-25109 are among the identifiers. Several of the issues allow unauthenticated, root-level remote code execution on the controller. The finding that makes this a food-safety story rather than an IT one is the demonstrated scenario: an attacker disables refrigeration while the temperature display continues to show normal readings, so the supervisory system that would normally raise the alarm is the same system telling you everything is fine. This is coordinated disclosure — both vendors have shipped fixes and no exploitation has been reported.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Claroty Team82 research — via Industrial Cyber

items.title: July recap: Coca-Cola’s fairlife suspended US dairy production for a ransomware incident, and had most capacity back inside two weeks
items.content_text: Carried here as context, not as news — this is a July event and nothing has changed on it since 27 July. Coca-Cola confirmed that its fairlife dairy business suspended production across four US sites after a ransomware intrusion detected in mid-July; Canadian operations were unaffected. The Anubis group claimed it had encrypted servers and taken roughly a terabyte of data. Coca-Cola reported most capacity restored by the end of the month and said it did not expect a material financial impact. The reason it stays on the page is the shape of the outage rather than its scale: what had to be rebuilt was the IT that plans, schedules, documents and releases production, not the control systems on the lines themselves. That is the same pattern Dragos describes across the whole quarter.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Coca-Cola statements and fairlife notices — via Cybersecurity Dive and BleepingComputer
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Incident detected 17 Jul 2026; most capacity restored 27 Jul 2026 — no update since

items.title: Eight Ceva Logistics warehouses stopped fulfilling for a week, and the delays reached retailers downstream
items.content_text: A cyberattack on Ceva Logistics between 29 July and 1 August disrupted contract logistics at eight European warehouses, delaying fulfilment for retail and e-commerce customers including Bol, De Bijenkorf and Ace & Tate; operations were still not fully restored by 6 August. Stolen data covers customer names, home addresses, email addresses, phone numbers and order details, with no payment data or credentials taken according to Ceva, and the Dutch data protection authority is investigating. No food business is named, but the pattern is the one that matters to this sector: third-party warehousing and transport is where most food companies’ finished goods sit, and a week of unavailable fulfilment against short-dated stock is spoilage, not just delay.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Ceva Logistics customer notifications — via The Record, TechCrunch and SecurityWeek
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Attack 29 Jul–1 Aug 2026; data-theft detail reported 10–11 Aug 2026

items.title: Food and beverage took 70 industrial ransomware incidents last quarter — and not one attacker reached a control system
items.content_text: Dragos recorded 1,140 ransomware incidents against industrial organisations in the second quarter of 2026, up 12 percent on the 1,020 it counted in the first. Food and beverage accounted for 70 of them, within a total dominated by manufacturing at 747. The number worth carrying into a management conversation is a zero: Dragos found no case in the quarter where a ransomware operator reached Stage 2 of the ICS Cyber Kill Chain or directly manipulated a control system. Its food-sector worked example is Mackay Sugar in Australia, where two mills stopped in June with no evidence that attackers reached ICS. Production halts in this data set cascade from virtualisation and ERP compromise, which is precisely why the vCenter and remote-access items further down this page matter more to a plant than their CVSS scores suggest.

items.title: Medusa has passed 500 critical-infrastructure victims, and it is weaponising new vulnerabilities within a day
items.content_text: CISA and the FBI refreshed their #StopRansomware advisory on Medusa on 18 August. The cumulative victim count across critical infrastructure passed 500 as of April 2026, up from roughly 300 in the March 2025 version — about 200 new victims in a year. Named target sectors include critical manufacturing, healthcare, the defense industrial base, government facilities, IT and financial services; the impact described is enterprise-IT encryption plus data theft, with no control-system involvement alleged. The operationally useful finding is speed: the group weaponises newly disclosed vulnerabilities within roughly 24 hours, and has been observed using exploits up to a week before public disclosure, because it buys them rather than developing them. Any exposure window measured in weeks of change control is therefore a real one.

items.title: The Iranian-affiliated PLC campaign is cooling, and no food or agriculture operator has been confirmed as a victim
items.content_text: Joint advisory AA26-097A, issued 7 April by the FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE, US Cyber Command’s Cyber National Mission Force and Treasury and expanded on 22 July, describes Iranian-affiliated actors reaching internet-exposed programmable logic controllers across US critical infrastructure. Confirmed victims remain water systems — at least 12 states, with more than 30 in Minnesota — and there has been no new confirmed victim since 14 August, no new named utility and no escalation. No food processor, grain co-operative or agricultural operator has been confirmed compromised. It stays on this page for one reason: no vulnerability is being exploited. The way in is a controller answering from the internet with a default, shared or absent password, and remote food and agriculture assets — outlying elevators, irrigation controls, cellular-connected pump and dryer skids — are exactly where that configuration survives.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA/FBI joint advisory AA26-097A and subsequent agency statements
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Issued 7 Apr 2026, expanded 22 Jul 2026; last confirmed victim activity 14 Aug 2026

items.title: A CVSS 10.0 command injection gives unauthenticated root on Haiwell’s IoT Cloud HMI gateway
items.content_text: CISA advisory ICSA-26-225-02 covers CVE-2026-19188, an OS command injection in the Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway rated 10.0. The Net Check feature reached through the /setting endpoint passes user input from the cmdPing Socket.io event straight to the operating system, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker run commands as root. Version 3.40.1.12 is affected; Haiwell has published Scada-v3.50.1.19. Gateways of this class reach food sites inside packaged equipment — a filler, a depalletiser, a blast chiller, a grain dryer, an irrigation controller — specified by the machine builder rather than by a controls standard, connected for remote support, and rarely present in any asset register.

items.title: SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced exposes Node-RED with no authentication — maximum-severity remote code execution
items.content_text: Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-834709, published 11 August, covers SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed. CVE-2026-58115 is rated CVSS 10.0 under both v3.1 and v4.0: the Node-RED HTTP interface enforces no authentication at all, so a remote unauthenticated attacker can create flows using programming nodes that execute system commands, giving arbitrary code execution at maximum privilege on the gateway. Every version before V4.3.4.1 is affected; the alternatives to updating are uninstalling Node-RED or hardening it per Node-RED’s own guidance. Worth noting that this one has no corresponding CISA ICSA advisory, so a team that tracks only ICS-CERT will not see it. In food and beverage these gateways typically arrive as part of an OEE, downtime-tracking or digitalisation project, bridging line equipment to a reporting platform — trusted by the control network, installed by an integrator, and almost never included in a patch schedule afterwards.

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Published 11 Aug 2026 — no corresponding CISA ICSA advisory

items.title: CISA added the exploited vCenter flaw to KEV yesterday — 361 hosts compromised across 47 countries
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-59310, a path-traversal flaw in VMware vCenter Server, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 18 August. Broadcom patched it on 29 July and exploitation began about five days later. German incident-response firm QUIRSO assesses with moderate confidence that a Chinese-speaking actor operates the campaign, counting around 361 affected addresses across 47 countries. The actor gains root on the vCenter appliance, plants a backdoor through cron and a reverse SSH binary, and in at least one case deployed Babuk-derived ransomware. Most food plants now run the historian, MES, SCADA nodes and label-print servers as virtual machines on one cluster, which makes the management plane a single point of failure for production and for traceability records at the same time.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalogue and QUIRSO research — via The Hacker News
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Patched 29 Jul 2026; exploitation from early Aug; added to KEV 18 Aug 2026

items.title: A Windows IKE flaw went into CISA’s KEV catalogue with a three-day federal deadline — it sits on the tunnels into your plants
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-33824, a double-free in the Microsoft Windows IKE service extensions (IKEEXT), to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 18 August with a federal remediation deadline of 21 August. A deadline that short signals confirmed exploitation at scale. IKE is the key-exchange half of IPsec, and IPsec is what terminates most site-to-site links and vendor remote access into food plants, distribution centres and cold stores — the tunnels used by machine builders, refrigeration service contractors and corporate IT. Remote code execution on the endpoint terminating those tunnels produces access that reads as ordinary maintenance in the logs, along the exact route that reaches line controls and utility systems. Three other flaws were added the same day, including a VMware vCenter path traversal and a SharePoint authentication bypass.

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Added to KEV 18 Aug 2026; remediation deadline 21 Aug 2026

items.title: Two building-automation advisories land on the systems that share infrastructure with plant refrigeration
items.content_text: Two of CISA’s 13 August advisories cover controls that in food plants and cold stores often sit on the same network and the same service contract as refrigeration. ICSA-26-225-08 covers Siemens Desigo DXR2 and PXC3, PXC4, PXC5 and PXC7 controllers: CVE-2026-59693, CVSS 4.3, lets malformed BACnet packets from an adjacent network crash the controller until it is reset or rebooted — a low score with an availability consequence in a facility where a controller reboot means an unmonitored space. Patched firmware is available for every affected model. ICSA-26-225-14 covers Johnson Controls Metasys, where CVE-2026-34491 (CVSS 8.0) is a persistent cross-site scripting flaw letting a low-privilege user plant a payload that runs in an administrator’s browser. Metasys 15 is patched at 15.0.1 and 16.0 ships fixed; versions 12 and 13 are end-of-support and can only be resolved by upgrading.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-225-08 (Siemens Desigo) and ICSA-26-225-14 (Johnson Controls Metasys)

items.title: Six flaws in Malcolm — CISA’s own OT traffic-analysis suite, and it usually sits inside the plant network
items.content_text: CISA published ICSA-26-230-01 on 18 August against Malcolm, its own open-source network-traffic-analysis suite for OT. Six flaws are listed, led by CVE-2026-55676 at CVSS 8.8, an unrestricted PHP file upload leading to arbitrary code execution; the rest cover path traversal on archive extraction (CVE-2026-63177, 7.1), two authorisation bypasses via unnormalised URI paths and percent-encoding, and resource-exhaustion denial of service. Versions below 26.06.1 and 26.07.0 and up to 26.07.1 are affected, with fixes in 26.07.0 and 26.08.0 depending on the CVE. There is no reported exploitation. It earns a place here because of where the software lives: food producers running a low-cost OT monitoring capability typically deploy Malcolm inside the plant network with a SPAN or TAP feed, which means broad visibility and a trusted position.

items.title: The new National Security Science and Technology Strategy names OT and ICS resilience as an explicit priority
items.content_text: The National Security Science and Technology Strategy was released on 19 August. Across its four pillars it names operational technology and industrial control system resilience, and technology supply chains, as explicit national priorities rather than leaving them inside a general cybersecurity heading. There is no regulatory requirement in it and nothing for an operator to comply with; it is a statement of research and investment direction. For food and agriculture the relevance is indirect but real — sector-specific OT security funding, research programmes and grant criteria tend to follow the language in documents like this one, and a strategy that separates OT resilience from IT security is easier to point at when arguing for a control-system budget line.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: National Security Science & Technology Strategy — via Industrial Cyber
